name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,187

clue.text: Greatest hero excited people looking for entertainment

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters get thrown into a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A star performer whips an audience into excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The two opening words supply exactly twelve letters, matching the enumeration, which is the tip-off that they are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Playgoers attend shows and performances, so they are an audience seeking an evening's amusement.

clue.text: I’m A Believer — record on random pile

indicators.note: random means in no set order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a record is a vinyl disc
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: The Monkees' hit single sits on top of a messy stack of records.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make the definition look like a song title; read plainly, it is someone declaring faith, a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a teacher or faith professes belief, so the statement describes such an adherent.

clue.text: Hairy man and son in water in France

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: eau is French for water
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A bearded father and his boy go swimming somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' inside 'water in France' is part of the phrase for EAU; the earlier 'in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's elder twin brother was born covered in hair, making him the Bible's famous hirsute figure.

clue.text: Act like bird and go away!

blocks.note: to act like something is to 'be a' one
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone is told to flap off like a bird and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: BE A TIT respaced becomes BEAT IT; 'Act like bird' suggests flapping or flying, but it means 'be a tit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang command tells someone to leave at once, the same as an impatient instruction to depart.

clue.text: Is learner involved in clever trick free?

indicators.note: being involved in something means being drawn inside it

blocks.note: a dodge is a cunning ruse
taken as written
L is the learner plate

explanation.surface: A question about whether a student caught up in a scam is in the clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective about the learner, but it is a verb meaning to prise loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something stuck is to work it loose from its position, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Reptile caught by fabulous bird

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant bird of legend

explanation.surface: A crocodile is snatched up by a mythical giant bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means 'of fable' here, not 'wonderful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The short informal name refers to a crocodile, a large scaly water-dwelling reptile.

clue.text: They may succeed in due course

definitions.text: They may succeed in due course

blocks.clueFragment: They may succeed in due course
blocks.note: surface reading: people who will do well eventually
setter's reading: succeed means follow on, taking over a title or estate

explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like 'achieve success', but it means 'come next in line', as with a throne or inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Successors in line to property or a title take over when the present holder dies, following them in due course.

clue.text: They leave their country, changing regimes

indicators.note: changing signals the letters are altered into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: People flee their homeland when governments change.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as political cause and effect, which hides that the letters of the last word are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles who settle abroad, often for political reasons, are people who have left their homeland.

clue.text: Having something in common with next door?

definitions.text: Having something in common with next door?

blocks.clueFragment: Having something in common with next door?
blocks.note: surface reading: sharing interests with the neighbours
setter's reading: the shared thing is a party wall between two houses

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like neighbourly friendship; the thing shared is literally a wall. In Britain this is the standard term for one of a pair of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a house is joined to one neighbour by a single shared wall, so it literally shares structure with next door.

clue.text: Story a nobleman heard

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone overheard a tale about an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the article and the title run together into a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative report of events, as in giving one's version, is a synonym for a tale or story.

clue.text: See Conservative beginning to upset male stand-in

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: lo is an old word for 'look' or 'see'
C abbreviates Conservative
opening letter of the word
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A political tale: watch a Tory start to annoy a man filling in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but only supplies its first letter. The Conservatives are Britain's main right-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or cleric temporarily covering for another is a substitute, the Latin-derived term for a temporary replacement.

clue.text: Given a new coat?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone has received a fresh jacket
setter's reading: a coat is a layer of paint

explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests clothing, but here it is a layer of paint on a wall or door.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a fresh layer of colour to a surface is giving it another coating of paint.

clue.text: One set of religious books completed as planned

definitions.note: the answer is a participle; 'as planned' is an adverbial phrase of similar meaning

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament
something completed has ended

explanation.surface: Someone finished a scripture collection exactly on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old and New Testaments are each a collection of books, so NT is the 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: What was meant or designed to happen is deliberate, matching something done according to a plan.

clue.text: Stuck in America, dreadfully bad person

indicators.note: something stuck in a phrase is embedded within its letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rotten character is stranded in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between the words is ignored when reading the letters through.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned term for a man who behaves dishonourably, especially towards women, so a scoundrel.

clue.text: Ceremonially installing knight with boasting all round

indicators.note: being all round something means surrounding it on every side

blocks.note: crowing is gloating or bragging
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is dubbed at a ceremony amid much self-congratulation.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess uses N for knight because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronation formally places a new monarch on the throne by placing the regal headpiece on them.

clue.text: Winning the prize ultimately? Wow!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so final letters are kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An excited reaction to taking home the trophy at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' reads as 'in the end, eventually' but picks out the final letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or amazement, interchangeable in casual American-style speech.

clue.text: Happened to be banished

blocks.note: first meaning: proved to be the case
second meaning: expelled or thrown out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Happened to be' reads as a single phrase, but the clue splits after the first word, with 'to be' merely joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both that events developed a certain way and that someone was evicted or expelled.

clue.text: Tell family member, one very small being ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a relative is a member of one's family
Roman numeral one
V abbreviates very; 'small' completes the surface

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a story about a family member whose tiny child was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed pair, IV, sits in the middle of the family word, not at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or narrate events to someone is to tell them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Some princess ending in German city

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a part of it, here a run of its letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A royal story finishes in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a major industrial city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is in North Rhine-Westphalia, in western Germany's Ruhr region, historically a steel centre.

clue.text: Evade southern invader

blocks.note: S abbreviates southern
the Huns invaded Europe in the fifth century

explanation.surface: Avoid the raider coming from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Invader is a historical example: the Huns under Attila.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from or avoid someone deliberately is to steer clear of them.

clue.text: Taciturn prisoner in American city ignored curfew initially

indicators.note: initially means at first, so the first letters are kept
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
opening letters of the two words
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped jailbird in a US city stayed out past curfew.
explanation.walkthrough: The city and the two initials join to make the container, with the convict going between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Using very few words, like the famously terse Spartans of Laconia, means being reserved in speech.

clue.text: Desperately want to leave king’s underground chamber

indicators.note: something that leaves is no longer there, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to crave is to long for
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch longs to escape from his dungeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king's' reads as possessive but stands for 'king is', i.e. R is to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural hollow in rock or beneath the ground is a subterranean chamber, the defining sense.

clue.text: Learner in hospital department trailing after boss

indicators.note: trailing after means following behind, setting the order of parts

blocks.note: a stud is a raised knob or boss, as on a shield
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A trainee on a hospital ward follows the senior doctor around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a superior, but it is a decorative stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying at a school or university is a pupil, someone who is acquiring knowledge.

clue.text: Goddess shortened end of programme in sports stadium maybe

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the last letter is lopped off
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Venus, Roman goddess of love, minus her final letter
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A star cut her show short in an arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the definition as an example: a stadium is one kind of event location.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where an event such as a match or concert is held, and a stadium is one example.
